- **Six new tokenized equities:** Amazon, Microsoft, Strategy, SanDisk, SpaceX, and Tesla
- **Total now live:** 10 tokenized stocks on Base
- **Access limits:** Eligible non-U.S. users only
- **Core trade-off:** More flexibility, more legal and liquidity risk
Coinbase Launches Tokenized Stocks on Ethereum Layer-2 on Sept. 4, expanding the lineup just 11 days after the first launch on Aug. 24. The initial batch included Apple, Alphabet, Meta, and Nvidia. Now the roster stretches across some of the biggest names in tech, plus Strategy, the bitcoin-heavy corporate treasury company that has become its own kind of cult asset in crypto circles.
The new tickers are AMZNc, MSFTc, MSTRc, SNDKc, SPCXc, and TSLAc. They trade on Base, Coinbase’s Ethereum layer-2 network, which is built to offer lower fees and faster settlement than Ethereum mainnet. That makes sense for assets Coinbase wants to move like financial primitives rather than dusty brokerage receipts.
But “tokenized stock” is the phrase that matters, not the ticker symbol alone. These assets are not ordinary shares sitting in a brokerage account under your name. Coinbase describes them as tokenized exposures tied to a legal and custody structure, not as a neat blockchain replacement for direct stock ownership. That distinction is the whole ballgame.
Tokenized equities are blockchain-based tokens that represent economic exposure to shares or equity interests in companies. In plain English: you get a token that tracks or mirrors the value of an offchain asset, but the rights you actually have depend on the issuer’s structure, custody model, and jurisdiction. The chain handles the transfer. The law decides what the token means.
That legal wrapper matters because Coinbase says the products are available only to eligible investors and not to U.S. persons. They are offered under Regulation S, which is a U.S. securities law exemption for offers and sales made outside the United States. It is not a loophole that turns securities into permissionless internet money. It is a limited framework, and the limits matter.

TL;DR:
Coinbase deployed six new tokenized stocks on its Layer-2 network Base . The initiative allows fractional shares of major technology and corporate firms to be traded in decentralized environments.
6 new Coinbase Tokenized Stocks just dropped
Amazon, Microsoft, Strategy, SanDisk, SpaceX, and Tesla are live on Base pic.twitter.com/ywHowwlvFq
— Base (@base) September 4, 2026
Following this update, network users gain access to contracts tied to Amazon, Tesla , Microsoft, SpaceX, SanDisk, and Strategy . These six assets join the initial rollout cohort consisting of Apple, Nvidia, Meta, and Alphabet , bringing the total catalog to ten available equities.
The addition of SpaceX stands out in particular due to its status as a private company not listed on traditional retail exchanges. Base’s official documentation specifies that the newly added shares are issued in digital format to enable holding within self-custodial wallets.
This expansion responds to results recorded during the initial issuance batch. On-chain metrics logged $227.7 million in cumulative trading volume across the first four equities.
Market analysts suggest that this initial liquidity supported accelerating the corporate timeline to broaden the offering.
The on-chain ecosystem supports 24/7 continuous trading for these instruments through decentralized platforms such as Aerodrome . Technical reports note that trading operates independently of traditional Wall Street market hours.
The underlying technical framework relies on a direct collateral model. Every token minted on Base is backed 1:1 by underlying shares held in custody by regulated broker Alpaca .
Legal issuance operates under the financial framework of the Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) . According to regulatory disclosures provided by the platform, the product is geographically restricted and strictly excludes U.S. resident investors.

# Coinbase Expands Offerings with Six New Tokenized Stocks Following $228M Launch - Daily Star
Coinbase has introduced six new tokenized stocks, featuring Amazon, Microsoft, and Tesla, to Base, following an impressive $227.7 million in trade volume on its initial offerings within roughly a month.
Summary
- Six additional equity tokens have been launched alongside the initial four on Coinbase’s Base platform.
- The new lineup includes Amazon, Microsoft, Strategy, SanDisk, SpaceX, and Tesla.
- Token Terminal recorded a decentralized exchange volume of $227.7 million for Coinbase-issued stock tokens over the last 30 days.
- Currently, U.S. investors are unable to access these products under Coinbase’s Regulation S offering.
As of Sept. 4, Base announced the availability of Amazon (AMZNc), Microsoft (MSFTc), Strategy (MSTRc), SanDisk (SNDKc), SpaceX (SPCXc), and Tesla (TSLAc) on-chain, broadening Coinbase’s range of tokenized equities shortly after the initial launch.
The introduction allows qualified investors to gain exposure to five publicly traded companies and the privately-owned SpaceX via tokens that can be transferred across supported platforms on the Ethereum layer-2 network. This setup enables developers to incorporate these assets into trading, lending, and other financial offerings designed for Base.

# Aave on Base launches tokenized stock collateral for USDC borrowing
Decentralized finance lending is expanding further into tokenized real-world assets as Aave V4 on Base opens a new market tied to public equities. The new Equities Hub lets eligible users outside the U.S. borrow USDC against seven Coinbase-issued tokenized stocks in permitted jurisdictions.
## Highlights
- Aave V4 on Base launched tokenized stocks of Apple, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Tesla as collateral for USDC borrowing, with collateral-only status at launch.
- The market starts with a $29 million initial collateral cap, $32 million USDC supply cap, and $21 million USDC borrow cap, with collateral factors between 65% and 79%.
- Aave targets institutional demand and expanding tokenized asset offerings, integrating Chainlink feeds with global equities access and noting $3.6 trillion cumulative deposits and $1 trillion in all-time loans.
## Equities hub structure and launch terms
As reported by The Block, the market went live Friday with tokenized versions of Apple, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla available as collateral in Aave V4 on Base.
Aave says users can deposit the tokenized stocks and take out USDC loans against them, while the assets remain collateral-only at launch. Chainlink provides onchain pricing through its tokenized equity feeds, and the protocol uses its Hub and Spoke architecture to combine the equity collateral into a single market with one USDC reserve.
According to Aave risk provider LlamaRisk, the market starts with an initial collateral cap of about $29 million across the seven stocks, a $32 million USDC supply cap and a $21 million USDC borrow cap. Collateral factors range from 65% to 79%, depending on the stock, and risk parameters are set separately for each asset so any issue affecting one equity is isolated from the others.

Coinbase Launches Tokenized Stocks on Aave V4, Backed by Seven Tech Giants
Table of Contents
Coinbase launched its tokenized stocks on the Aave V4 protocol , deployed on the Base network. This integration allows tokenized shares of U.S. technology companies to be used as collateral to take out loans in USDC .
The available assets are seven: AAPLc, AMZNc, GOOGLc, METAc, MSFTc, NVDAc and TSLAc , each backed by real shares held in custody by Alpaca Securities LLC , a broker-dealer registered with the SEC, in segregated accounts maintained in the name of the issuer.
Chainlink operates as the official oracle solution, supplying market data through tokenized equity feeds active Sunday through Friday during market hours.
Each token represents a certificate issued by Coinbase Onchain SPV Ltd. and grants direct economic exposure to the underlying share, without synthetic references. Dividends are automatically reinvested and stock splits are processed through an onchain multiplier, making each token a total return instrument.
The Aave market operates 24 hours a day, although affected reserves are paused during corporate actions until the new multiplier is applied. Looking ahead to the next stages, incorporating GHO as a borrowable asset is expected, along with an expansion of the tokenized stock list available on Coinbase, subject to governance and risk review.
